chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Ja'far from his father (peace be upon them both) that Ali (peace be upon him) said:

When a man marries a woman, her daughter becomes forbidden to him if he consummates the marriage with the mother; but if he does not consummate with the mother, there is no harm in him marrying the daughter. And if he marries the daughter and consummates with her or does not consummate with her, the mother becomes forbidden to him. And he said: 'Stepdaughters are forbidden to you, whether they are in your custody or not.'
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions under which a daughter becomes forbidden to her mother's husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the asymmetry in marital prohibitions: while consummation with a mother prohibits her daughter, mere marriage to a daughter (without consummation) is sufficient to prohibit the mother, reflecting the principle of *al-nikah yuharrim al-umm*. It further establishes the permanent prohibition of stepdaughters (*al-raba'ib*) regardless of cohabitation, a key distinction in Shia jurisprudence regarding the completeness of the family bond. This narration underscores the legal weight of the marriage contract itself in establishing *mahram* relationships.
